record.context_brief: Prime decompositions in non-Archimedean Banach spaces
record.original_question: Let E be a finite-dimensional Banach space over a non-Archimedean valued field. Call a nonzero subspace E₁ of E prime if there is no proper subspace E₂ of E such that E is the orthogonal direct sum of E₁ and E₂. Every finite-dimensional Banach space can be decomposed as an orthogonal direct sum of prime subspaces. Is this prime decomposition unique in a natural sense?

evidence.quote: A non-zero subspace \(E\_ 1\) of a Banach space \(E\) is said to be prime if there is no proper subspace \(E\_ 2\) of \(E\) such that \(E\) is the orthogonal direct sum of \(E\_ 1\) and \(E\_ 2\). Every finite-dimensional Banach space can be decomposed as an orthogonal direct sum of prime subspaces. Is the prime decomposition unique in a natural sense?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $K$ be a field equipped with a non-trivial non-Archimedean absolute value $|\cdot|$, and let $E$ be a finite-dimensional Banach space over $K$ (with norm $\|\cdot\|$). Two nonzero subspaces $E_1, E_2 \subseteq E$ are said to be orthogonal, and $E$ is called the orthogonal direct sum $E_1 \perp E_2$, if $E = E_1 \oplus E_2$ as a vector space and
$$\|x_1 + x_2\| = \max(\|x_1\|,\|x_2\|) \quad \text{for all } x_1 \in E_1,\ x_2 \in E_2.$$
A nonzero subspace $E_1 \subseteq E$ is called prime if there is no proper nonzero subspace $E_2 \subseteq E$ such that $E = E_1 \perp E_2$ (equivalently, $E_1$ admits no nontrivial orthogonal complement in $E$, except $E_1 = E$ itself which is allowed).

It is known that every finite-dimensional non-Archimedean Banach space $E$ admits a decomposition
$$E = P_1 \perp P_2 \perp \cdots \perp P_n$$
as an orthogonal direct sum of prime subspaces $P_1,\ldots,P_n$.

Question: Is such a prime decomposition unique in a natural sense? More precisely, given two prime orthogonal decompositions
$$E = P_1 \perp \cdots \perp P_n = Q_1 \perp \cdots \perp Q_m,$$
must one have $n = m$ and a permutation $\sigma$ of $\{1,\ldots,n\}$ together with isometric isomorphisms $P_i \cong Q_{\sigma(i)}$ (and ideally an isometric automorphism of $E$ carrying one decomposition to the other)?
artifact.status_search_result: A web search for results on uniqueness of prime orthogonal decompositions of finite-dimensional non-Archimedean Banach spaces did not return any source explicitly resolving the question. Related work concerns the (orthogonal) finite-dimensional decomposition property in non-Archimedean Banach spaces, but no definitive statement of a uniqueness theorem (or counterexample) for the prime decomposition was located.

status_evidence.title: The Finite-dimensional Decomposition Property in Non-Archimedean Banach Spaces
status_evidence.snippet: A non-Archimedean Banach space has the orthogonal finite-dimensional decomposition property (OFDDP) if it is the orthogonal direct sum of a sequence of finite-dimensional subspaces.
status_evidence.claim: Related literature studies orthogonal finite-dimensional decompositions in non-Archimedean Banach spaces, but does not explicitly address uniqueness of prime decompositions.

status_evidence.title: The finite-dimensional decomposition property for non-Archimedean Banach spaces
status_evidence.snippet: Survey-style notes on orthogonal decomposition properties of non-Archimedean Banach spaces.
status_evidence.claim: Recent expository material on decompositions of non-Archimedean Banach spaces does not appear to settle the prime decomposition uniqueness question.
